company_name: Foshan Haitian Flavouring and Food Company Ltd.

inputs.share_count_basis: 5,851.825m total issued shares (A + H) per H1 2026 interim report, held FLAT. Includes 11.07m treasury shares held for the 2024/2025 employee stock ownership plans (these will be awarded, so they are counted rather than netted). H1 2026 note 9(b): no dilutive potential ordinary shares; FY2025 diluted weighted average 5,701.98m only differed from basic by the H-share over-allotment option, since exercised. SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so no further dilution is charged (charge-once rule).
inputs.cash_composition: 30 June 2026 (RMB m): cash and cash equivalents 5,137.134 + term deposits and certificates of deposit 20,030.686 (current 13,788.089 + non-current 6,242.597; note 15(b), terms over three months, held with banks) + bank-issued wealth management products at FVPL 10,814.342 (note 11(i): variable return, redeemable on demand or short term). Restricted cash 13.849 and the RMB0.1m equity security excluded. The term deposits and WMPs are the H-share IPO proceeds (net RMB9,180m, June 2025) plus retained cash parked in bank instruments; they are treated as cash because (i) they are bank deposits/bank-issued short-dated products, not operating assets, and (ii) their income (interest income RMB687.9m and FVPL fair-value gains RMB235.7m in FY2025) is stripped from the projected EBITDA margin, satisfying the matching-asset rule.
inputs.total_debt_composition: Bank loans and other borrowing 357.35 (351.35 current + 6.0 non-current, all RMB, fixed rate) + lease liabilities 87.58 (36.161 current + 51.419 non-current), 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, consolidated cash flow note: 'Equity settled share-based payments' RMB162,896k (2024: nil); first year of the 2025 employee stock ownership plan. Equity-award taxes nil (A-share ESOP, no net-share settlement). FY2024 SBC was nil.
inputs.interest_income_note: Under the HKFRS presentation Haitian uses, interest income (FY2025 P&L RMB687.9m; cash received RMB557.9m) is removed from 'cash generated from operations' and interest received is shown in INVESTING activities, so reported_fcf (OCF 7,745.951 - capex 1,283.600 = 6,462.351) already excludes it. Deducting it again would strip it twice; interest_income is therefore 0 in the last_fcf identity. The P&L interest income (687.9) and the FVPL fair-value gains (235.7) ARE stripped from the forward EBITDA margin anchor so the RMB35.98bn cash pile is counted once, in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 and H1 2026: no repurchases (FY2024: RMB313.8m bought back for the ESOP). Flat count is a modelling convention funded by the RMB162.9m SBC expense, not by current buybacks; the company distributes through dividends (>=80% payout commitment FY2025-27, RMB6,424.8m paid in H1 2026).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); H-share quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1743 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-22T07:17Z. Parity check: the A-share 603288.SS closed at RMB33.47 (2026-10-22), = HK$39.30 at this rate, against the H-share quote at inputs.price_as_of -- the H-share trades at a ~33% discount to the A-share, which is the normal A-H discount for a mainland consumer name, not an FX-direction error. All per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD at 1.1743 for the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv; CNY twins carry the _cny suffix. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate -- re-check CNYHKD on each refresh.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T07:03:08Z (intraday HKEX print, ~15:03 HKT; replace at the regular close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY: China 10-year government bond ~1.8%, China equity risk premium ~6.5%, staples beta ~0.8-0.9 gives a cost of equity of ~7.0-7.5%; the capital structure is effectively all-equity (RMB0.4bn of borrowings against RMB36bn of cash). Rounded UP to 8.0% to carry a governance/disclosure and A-H structural discount for a mainland Chinese issuer in the rate rather than in an ad-hoc scenario premium. Same 8.0% in all three scenarios -- risk is charged once, in the flows via the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt: lease liabilities (RMB87.6m) are inside total_debt; lease principal (H1 2026 RMB23.9m) is NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use asset renewal is already inside the capex line because Haitian's investing-activities capex line is 'payment for purchase of property, plant and equipment, right-of-use assets and intangible assets'. Right-of-use depreciation (RMB47.8m FY2025) is inside D&A and added back like any other D&A. Immaterial either way (<0.3% of EBITDA).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests RMB510.5m (30 June 2026) deducted at book in the equity bridge. NCI's profit share is negligible (RMB0.3m in H1 2026, RMB7.8m in H1 2025) so the flows are modelled on a consolidated basis and NOT additionally leaked; deducting the full book value is the conservative single charge (~RMB0.09/share).
inputs.ebitda_anchor: FY2025 reported EBITDA (CSV) RMB9,457.6m = profit from operations 8,620.9 + D&A 836.6. Adjusted to an OPERATING, PRE-SBC basis: - interest income 687.9 - FVPL fair-value gains 235.7 (both non-operating, their source assets sit in the bridge) + SBC 162.9 (the engine deducts SBC separately) + net FX loss 204.3 (one-off translation loss on the HKD IPO proceeds) = RMB8,901.2m = 30.8% of revenue. Government grants and VAT additional deductions (RMB159m) are left in as recurring. Year-1 (FY2026) margin set at 31.0%: H1 2026 gross margin +0.9pp YoY (41.0%) on the soybean cost tailwind, partly reinvested in selling/marketing (+18.7% in FY2025).
inputs.cash_tax_anchor: FY2025 income tax RMB1,550.0m on PBT 8,595.4 = 18.0% effective; cash tax paid 1,401.8 (16.3%). Removing the ~25% tax on the non-operating interest/FVPL income gives ~17.2% on operating EBIT. The parent enjoys the 15% High and New Technology Enterprise rate; subsidiaries pay 25%. Base 17.5% flat; bear 20% (HNTE status lapses); bull 17%.
inputs.working_capital_anchor: Distributors pay in advance (contract liabilities RMB4,128m at FY2025; trade receivables only RMB274m), so growth releases cash: FY2025 cash generated from operations 9,147.8 vs operating pre-SBC EBITDA ex non-operating income ~8,901 implies ~RMB200-250m inflow on a RMB1,969m revenue increase, ~10-12% capture. Base 8%, bull 10%, bear 0% (H1 2026 OCF fell 18.5% on procurement timing -- a reminder the inflow is not guaranteed).
inputs.balance_sheet_timing_note: Flows are projected from FY2025 (FY0) while the net-cash anchor is the 30 June 2026 balance sheet, i.e. AFTER the RMB6,424.8m of FY2025 final + special dividends paid in H1 2026 and after H1 2026 owner FCF of ~RMB0.7bn. The half-year FCF is thus double-counted by ~RMB0.12/share -- immaterial, and conservative in direction because the H1 dividend outflow is fully reflected.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, non-US consumer staples -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md, read in full). Haitian is a cash-generative, net-cash condiment manufacturer with an owner-FCF stream that is well defined, so the default engine applies; the adaptations used are (a) CNY-built WACC and the CNY->HKD bridge, (b) lease treatment A, (c) NCI deducted once in the bridge, (d) matching-asset rule for the RMB36bn deposit/WMP pile, (e) near-SBC-zero market -- SBC is 0.56% of revenue so house and street almost coincide. First valuation of this ticker (no prior Drivers/DCF). Horizon 10 years (FY2026-FY2035): margins are mature already but the growth path decelerates from ~6% to 3% over the decade, so the terminal year is capitalised on a settled growth rate. No numeric FY2026 guidance exists (Analysis.json guidance block); year-1 growth is set from the H1 2026 run-rate (+6.0%). Price is an intraday HKEX print.

equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 interim balance sheet; NCI profit share negligible so flows are not separately leaked

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2025 revenue growth (+7.3%) and H1 2026 run-rate (+6.0%), haircut toward the Frost & Sullivan China condiments market CAGR of ~6.2%; equity CAGR is unusable as a growth source because FY2025 book value is inflated by the RMB9.2bn H-share IPO
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity +33.8% YoY vs revenue +7.3% and EPS +7.9%: divergence is the June 2025 H-share IPO proceeds, not operating growth. Owner-FCF +19.7% (5,264 -> 6,299 on a consistent SBC-adjusted, interest-excluded basis) outpaced revenue because FY2025 capex fell to 4.4% of revenue from 5.9%; SBC went from nil to 0.56% of revenue so a small part of reported growth is now paid in stock.
historical_growth.notes: The folder's Metrics.csv holds H-share filings only (H1 2024 onward), so 3- and 5-year CAGRs cannot be computed from house data. For context only, the A-share annual reports (603288.SH, not in this folder) show revenue of roughly RMB22.8bn (FY2020), 25.0bn (FY2021), 25.6bn (FY2022), 24.5bn (FY2023), 26.9bn (FY2024): a ~4.8% 5-year and ~4.1% 3-year revenue CAGR including the FY2023 reset. Owner-FCF series used for the 1-year growth: FY2024 5,263.971 - 0 SBC = 5,264.0; FY2025 6,462.351 - 162.896 = 6,299.5 (interest already outside OCF in both years).

base.narrative: Domestic core categories grow mid-single digits with premium/health lines and the catering channel adding ~1pp; overseas and Amoy are too small to move the total before FY2029. Soybean tailwind lifts gross margin but is partly reinvested in marketing, so operating EBITDA margin drifts up only 1pp over the decade. Capex normalises from the 4.4% FY2025 level toward 3.5% once the Indonesia/Vietnam bases are built.

bull.narrative: The internationalisation plan works: Amoy's 30-country distribution, halal lines and the SE Asian plants take overseas to a meaningful share of revenue by FY2030, compound condiments and vinegar/cooking wine scale on the existing channel, and the Lighthouse-factory cost gap versus Qianhe/Jonjee widens so the commodity tailwind is retained as margin (operating EBITDA margin to 34%). Higher early capex funds the overseas bases.

bear.narrative: Chinese consumption stays soft, edible-oil majors (Arawana, Luhua) and Qianhe's zero-additive positioning force promotional spend, and soybean/wheat prices revert from multi-year lows as they did in 2021-22, compressing the operating EBITDA margin 2.5pp. Overseas and Amoy absorb capital without reaching scale, the HNTE 15% tax status lapses, and the distributor-prepayment working-capital tailwind stops. Growth settles at 2%.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-single-digit domestic growth (soy/oyster/flavoured sauce ~77% of revenue) with premiumisation and catering-channel gains; margin up ~1pp over the decade as the soybean tailwind is partly reinvested; overseas is optionality, not the plan.
scenario_narratives.bull: Overseas (Amoy, SE Asian plants, halal lines) and adjacent categories lift growth to ~8% for five years and the cost moat holds the commodity tailwind as margin (34% operating EBITDA).
scenario_narratives.bear: Soft Chinese consumption, promotional competition from adjacent-category entrants, and a commodity reversal cut growth to ~2% and margins by 2.5pp while overseas capex earns nothing.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 20/55/25. Bull weight down because the bull case needs three independent things -- overseas execution by a company with no track record outside China, adjacent-category scaling, and the soybean tailwind persisting -- all to land. Bear weight up to 20% for the China consumption macro and the demonstrated 2021-23 episode (revenue fell in FY2023, margins compressed on the commodity spike) rather than for any solvency risk: the balance sheet is RMB36bn net cash. Base is the house view: a mature staples compounder with a wide cost moat.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Haitian is valued as a mature, net-cash consumer-staples compounder: owner FCF (reported FCF less the RMB163m SBC charge; interest already sits outside OCF under HKFRS presentation) is projected from components over ten years at an 8% CNY WACC and capitalised at min(Gordon 2.5%, 20x). The RMB36bn of cash, term deposits and bank WMPs is added once in the bridge, with its income stripped from the margin. Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD at 1.1743; the H-share trades at a ~33% discount to the A-share, so an H-share buyer is paying materially less for the same cash flows than the A-share market implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net cash is ~RMB6.1/share (HK$7.1), roughly a quarter of the H-share price: the valuation depends on that cash being returned (the >=80% payout commitment supports this) rather than deployed into low-return overseas M&A.
Terminal value is ~60% of EV at an 8% WACC; every 1pp on the CNY discount rate is worth roughly 15% of the equity value.
The operating EBITDA margin anchor (30.8%) strips FY2025 interest/FVPL income and adds back a RMB204m FX loss; if the FX loss recurs on unhedged HKD proceeds the anchor is ~0.7pp too high.
A-H discount: the HKD value per share is not comparable to the A-share price; a narrowing of the discount is a re-rating, not a change in intrinsic value.
Commodity reversal (soybean, wheat, packaging) is the main margin risk; the bear case carries 2.5pp of compression, the 2021-22 episode was ~4pp on gross margin.
No numeric FY2026 guidance exists; year-1 growth rests on the H1 2026 run-rate.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (intraday HKEX print); 52-week range 25.00-38.38. A-share 603288.SS and CNYHKD=X from the same endpoint for the parity check.
data_sources.financials: 3288.HK_Metrics.csv (H1 2024 - H1 2026, RMB m) built from the FY2025 annual report and H1 2026 interim report; balance-sheet anchors (cash, term deposits, FVPL WMPs, borrowings, lease liabilities, NCI, shares) read directly from the H1 2026 interim report (3288.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt lines 2776-2865, 2955-2995, 3460-3530, 3735-3765); SBC, interest income, FVPL gains, FX loss and D&A from the FY2025 annual report (3288.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt lines 6985-7012, 9340-9410, 9510-9530, 10989).
data_sources.qualitative: 3288.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-22): business model, moat factors, growth drivers, bull/bear cases, Frost & Sullivan market CAGR, FY2025-27 dividend policy.
